thread:
incident-bot: [PAGE] sev2 -> Observed sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate for /v1/generate on us-west-2. p95 token latency increased ~2.3x since 2026-03-15T15:42:10Z. Alert dashboards: https://internal-graphs/redwood/alerts/1767092468 :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: ack, I'm taking pager. Noted customer-visible latency and a few support tickets (TICKET-2034, TICKET-2035). Will gather impact and start timeline.

ben_sre: scope check — embeddings endpoints impacted or only text-gen?

alice_oncall: only text-gen route so far (/v1/generate). Quick metrics: prefix KV cache hit-rate fell from ~92% to ~14% across us-west-2 pool.

carla_runtime: pulling KV cache metrics now. Query I ran: `select bucket, prefix, hit_count, miss_count, ts from kv_cache_metrics where region='us-west-2' and prefix like '/v1/%' order by ts desc limit 200`

carla_runtime: log snippet pulled from serving nodes:
```
2026-03-15T15:41:58Z deploy-service: rollout v2.8.1 -> canary(us-west-2)
2026-03-15T15:42:10Z prefix-cache: insert key=/prefix/abc123 ttl=3600
2026-03-15T15:42:35Z prefix-cache: miss key=/prefix/abc123
2026-03-15T15:43:00Z proxy: p95=480ms, p50=120ms
2026-03-15T15:45:12Z prefix-cache: miss-rate spike start
```

dinesh_eng: I see a recent deploy change in the canary: env `KV_CACHE_REUSE` was set to `false` to avoid cross-model leakage during canary tests. That would prevent reuse of cached prefixes between model variants — plausible root cause for mass misses.

alice_oncall: can we toggle that back in canary? If it is the cause, we want to restore reuse asap.

carla_runtime: initiating env change rollback on canary: `kubectl set env deployment/model-canary KV_CACHE_REUSE=true -n serving`

deploy-bot: Rollout job started: deployment/model-canary env update by carla_runtime (job id roll-1767092475)

eve_support: customers: AcmeCorp and BetaApps reported elevated latencies and 504-like timeouts. Support has opened interim comms.

ben_sre: Starting emergency mitigation — triggering prefix warmers and temporary TTL relaxation. Command to kick off warmers: `POST /internal/serving/warm` with body {prefix:'/v1/generate', parallel:50}.

carla_runtime: executing warm job now:
```
$ curl -s -X POST 'https://internal-redwood/api/serving/warm' -d '{"prefix":"/v1/generate","parallel":50}'
{'status':'started','job_id':'warm-1767092468'}
```

carla_runtime: rolled KV_CACHE_REUSE back to true in canary at approx 2026-03-15T15:46:10Z.

ben_sre: watching metrics: hit-rate pre-change ~92%, dropped to 14% at 15:44, after env rollback + warmers: 15:53 -> 41%, 15:56 -> 76%, 15:58 -> 88%. p95 latency returned to baseline by 15:58.

alice_oncall: customer impact summary: 4 paying customers affected, median extra latency ~350ms, error rates up ~0.9% at peak. Logged incident id INC-2026-03-15-03.

dinesh_eng: candidate hypotheses (in-thread tracking):
- H1: `KV_CACHE_REUSE=false` in canary caused cross-model cache isolation, reducing reuse and causing a cold cache effect.
- H2: recent prefix-normalizer change during the same deploy introduced subtle key namespace shift (e.g., trimming/trailing slash behavior) so cached keys didn't match.
- H3: an unrelated invalidation flood (background job) evicted prefixes around the same time.

carla_runtime: I ran a diff on the canary deploy manifest: the only intentional changes were the env toggle and a whitespace change in prefix normalizer file (no functional changes expected). Attaching diff: https://internal-paste/diff-176709

ben_sre: evidence for H1: config toggle aligns with the timing. Evidence for H2: metric shows some prefixes still hit (not everything zero), and logs show entries of both normalized and non-normalized shapes during the window. I'll collect a sample set.

carla_runtime: sample query output (trimmed):
```
prefix            hit_count miss_count
/v1/generate      12000     17000   <-- large miss burst
/v1/generate/     4000      20      <-- some continued hits on alternate shape
```

alice_oncall: mitigation timeline (for timeline section in RCA):
- 15:41:58 - v2.8.1 rollout started (canary us-west-2)
- 15:42:10 - first diff shows KV_CACHE_REUSE=false applied to canary
- 15:44:30 - alert: prefix cache hit-rate drop, p95 up
- 15:46:10 - carla_runtime rolled KV_CACHE_REUSE back to true in canary
- 15:49:00 - warm job started (parallel=50)
- 15:55:00 - hit-rate >80%
- 15:58:00 - p95 latency returned to baseline; incident downgraded

frank_prod: customer comms draft: "Mitigation applied; service restored. We are investigating root cause and will follow up in 48 hours with a postmortem and action items." Will send after approval.

ben_sre: temporary follow-ups: 1) block deploys that change KV_CACHE_REUSE without explicit rollout gating, 2) add per-prefix hit-rate alert with absolute thresholds, 3) add canary warmers to run automatically when prefix-serving configs change.

dinesh_eng: I'll own deeper postmortem to confirm if prefix normalizer whitespace could have changed behavior; carla_runtime will reproduce locally against canary manifest. ben_sre owns mitigation verification.

alice_oncall: handoff: ben_sre primary for next 2 hours to finish instrumentation and final metrics dump. Then handoff to dinesh_eng for the RCA write-up. I'll update the incident tracker and close when postmortem created. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Severity update: downgraded to sev3 at 2026-03-15T15:58:12Z (note: service recovered).

carla_runtime: saved query outputs and logs uploaded: https://internal-paste/kv-metrics-176709 and https://internal-paste/serving-logs-176709

ben_sre: final timeline (to include in RCA): 15:41 deploy start, 15:42 config applied, 15:44 alert, 15:46 config rollback, 15:49 warmers, 15:55 hit-rate recovery, 15:58 p95 baseline.

alice_oncall: closing notes in thread: root cause hypothesis: KV_CACHE_REUSE toggle in canary (primary) possibly compounded by prefix normalization mismatch (secondary). Action items created in the incident board: 1) gating around cache-related env toggles (owner: eng-platform), 2) auto-run prefix warmers on deploy (owner: eng-runtime), 3) per-prefix hit-rate alert and dashboard (owner: eng-sre). ETA for postmortem: 48h.

eve_support: adding customer notes to impacted tickets and flagging for follow-up comms after postmortem.

frank_prod: merging comms once postmortem draft ready. :white_check_mark:
